newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom cuts sponsorship for Russian football team.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom cuts sponsorship for Russian football team.

text.p: The Russian national football side, struggling to turn talent into goals, suffered a new blow on Wednesday when Gazprom, Russia's biggest company and the teams's leading sponsor said it was slashing its funding.
Gazprom officials would not discuss the sums involved but soccer officials said the drop in sponsorship would cut the national federation's budget by a fifth to a quarter.
"Maybe if they played better, they might get more money," an official at Gazprom, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

Other officials declined to give a specific reason for the reduction in funding. One soccer federation source said it seemed rather the result of general belt-tightening at Gazprom, Russia's gas monopoly.

Gazprom owns about a quarter of the world's natural gas reserves and used to be headed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin. It has been under pressure lately to contribute more taxes to the government budget.

Vladimir Rodionov, director general of the Russian Soccer Union (RFS), said he still hoped for a change of heart from Gazprom, which has been pumping cash into the national squad and a number of league and junior sides for the past four years.
"I hope there are people in Gazprom who cannot turn their backs on Russian soccer and that this period of coolness will end," he told Reuters.

The Russian national side have promised much and delivered little but embarrassment since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1992. Hampered by a series of rows between players and a succession of managers, they were dumped out in the early stages of the 1994 World Cup finals and Euro 96.
They are, however, on course for a place in the 1998 World Cup finals in France and are top of their qualifying group.
